title: Span slice presets and compact viewer playbook (WIP)
content:
Purpose and scope:

This doc captures a focused riff on two complementary features we keep hearing about in CS and SRE interviews: 1) ‘Span slice’ presets (quickly isolate meaningful span groupings across traces), and 2) a compact/stacked waterfall mode for high-density browsing. Goal is to produce a minimal viable interaction spec + low-fidelity wireframe notes and a groomed backlog for an initial iteration (alpha) that can be shipped to Dedicated customers as an opt-in console flag.

User problems we are solving:
- Long traces (200+ spans) are painful to scan; engineers repeatedly create ad-hoc filters and lose context when time-shifting.
- Common investigative patterns repeat: focus on DB spans, external HTTP calls, or queue/worker boundaries. Users want canned slices that preserve context (parents, timeline) instead of blunt filters.
- Console list + waterfall view uses too much vertical space; compact rows that still show timings would accelerate triage.

High-level ideas / interaction primitives:

1) Span Slice Presets panel (left rail, collapsible)
- Presets are named slices: e.g., "DB-only (with parents)", "External HTTP + 2 hops", "Service boundary crossings", "queue/dequeue path".
- Each preset defines: span-kind filter (name/glob/tag), depth (0 = exact, 1 = parents+children up to N), time padding (ms before/after), and optional alignment rule (align to parent start / absolute time).
- Preset preview: hover shows a small sparkline of distribution of span durations and a sample mini-waterfall for the last n traces.
- Users can create/save/edit presets. First-run templates: DB, HTTP, Cache, Auth, Background Jobs.
- Sharing: presets can be team-scoped or personal (ACL). Short-term: personal only.

2) Compact stacked waterfall (main canvas toggle)
- Two modes: Standard (current) / Compact. Compact reduces vertical height of each span row (single-line with thin bar + chevrons for collapsed children).
- Visual affordances for density: small bars + inline duration labels on hover, color coded by span-kind. Mouseover still expands a detailed tooltip.
- Row grouping: adjacent spans with same service/span-kind can be collapsed into an axial cluster that indicates count (e.g., "x6"), expand on click.
- Keyboard navigation: j/k move selection between visible rows; right arrow dives into cluster (expand), left arrow collapses. Enter toggles open span details.

3) Preserve focus while time-shifting and switching presets
- When a slice is applied, console remembers the selected span (if visible) and tries to preserve selection if an analogous span exists after filter change. If not, fall back to nearest parent or previous timestamp.
- Time-shift scrubber should have a small indicator for the selected span’s original time so users can keep relative position when changing view.

Wireframe notes (low-fi) — layout expectations:
- Top bar: trace header + controls (search, open preset dropdown, time-shift scrubber, compact toggle).
- Left rail (collapsible 260px): presets list, create button, manage.
- Main canvas: timeline ruler at top (zoom + pan controls), waterfall area, events/annotations row (user bookmarks, errors, logs).
- Right side: details drawer (stacked tab: span metadata / logs / stacktrace / sample payloads).

Acceptance criteria (alpha):
- Create/read/update/delete (CRUD) for personal presets.
- Applying a preset filters the waterfall and populates timeline padding per preset settings.
- Compact mode reduces per-span height by >=40% and enables cluster collapse for consecutive similar spans.
- Keyboard navigation works in compact mode for selection and cluster expand/collapse.
- Preset hover shows sample mini-waterfall (client-side sample generation, cached).

Backlog (prioritized) — grooming estimates and owners:
- TRACE-101 Add left-rail presets UI + CRUD (2w) — owner: Lina Alvarez — deps: backend presets table (PLAT-88).
- TRACE-102 Preset semantics + apply engine (1.5w) — owner: Marco Chen — deps: runtime filter library (SERV-210).
- TRACE-103 Compact waterfall CSS + cluster collapse (1w) — owner: Samir Patel — note: must measure perf impact for 1k spans.
- TRACE-104 Keyboard nav and focus preservation (3d) — owner: Aditi Rao — test cases: selection persist across preset switch.
- TRACE-105 Preset sharing (team-scoped) + ACL (future) (2w) — owner: product to prioritize.

Open questions / design tradeoffs:
- Should presets be declarative or scriptable? (Scriptable allows precise selection but increases complexity.) Proposal: alpha uses declarative JSON model with text search + glob. Evaluate scriptable in 2H.
- Performance: generating mini-waterfalls on hover could be heavy. Start with sampled traces (last 50) and a cache with TTL 30s. If cost is high, revert to single example trace preview.
- Should compact mode be global or per-user? Prefer per-user toggle stored in preferences.
- How to handle pinned spans/logs when switching to a preset that removes them? Option: convert pins to bookmarks scoped to trace id + timestamp and show a banner when pins become hidden, with quick 'recenter' action.

Telemetry and metrics to measure success:
- Time-to-first-action while triaging (open trace -> apply preset -> inspect span) — target reduce by 25% vs baseline.
- % of traces where compact mode is used after feature launch.
- Preset creation rate and usage frequency (team vs personal).
- Keyboard nav adoption (key counts / selection changes).

Accessibility notes:
- Compact rows must still be readable: provide an option to increase row height.
- Keyboard-only workflows must allow full navigation of clusters and details drawer.
- Color contrast check for span-kind palettes; provide shape/glyph fallback.

Implementation risks & mitigations:
- Risk: runtime filtering semantics might produce surprising context loss (users lose parent spans). Mitigation: preset default includes parent+N children; surface a prominent "context lost" warning with quick revert.
- Risk: DOM too large for 1k spans in compact mode. Mitigation: virtualize rows (windowed rendering) + incremental render checks; perf regression test in SRE harness.

Next steps / immediate action items:
- [Lina] Draft initial React left-rail component and storybook knobs (due 2024-12-01).
- [Marco] Prototype filter apply logic in sandbox backend and share sample JSON schema (due 2024-11-28).
- [Samir] Build compact CSS prototype + perf test plan (due 2025-01-03).
- [Aditi] Write acceptance test matrix and a short UX walkthrough video (prototype) for internal review (due 2024-12-08).

Notes from recent feedback (customer sessions):
- "We keep opening traces, filtering down, and then wishing we had the parent to understand impact" — multiple enterprise users.
- "Compact mode is great if I can still get to logs quickly" — SRE teams.

Appendix: example preset JSON (declarative model) — alpha sketch (sample):
{
  "id": "db-with-parents",
  "name": "DB-only (with parents)",
  "filter": { "span_name_glob": "*sql*|*db*|*psql*", "tags": ["db.statement"] },
  "context_depth": 1,
  "time_padding_ms": 200,
  "alignment": "align-parent-start"
}

(Above JSON is for design reference only; actual storage may be per-user row in backend.)

If this direction looks good we should: 1) lock the preset JSON model, 2) implement alpha rails + apply behavior, 3) run perf tests on traces with 500–2000 spans.

End of doc.
